original_test_intent: Verify every required upper-fan status channel for the switch-board cooling domain, ensuring correct physical membership, sensor identity/description, status-or-reading semantics and consistency across SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web.
original_method: The thermal owner expands 1~N into actual upper-bank fan positions and stable SDR records, defines whether each is discrete status, presence/fault or analog RPM, supplies expected values and Web mapping, then automation collects complete passive IPMI evidence for per-member comparison.
manual_activity: The thermal/platform owner maps upper fan positions to sensor records, defines status/RPM semantics and expected values and confirms the Web rows. No SF600 hardware, fan manipulation or active fault is part of this sensor-list check.
required_inputs: Switch-board/chassis cooling topology and definition of the upper fan bank
Installed upper-fan positions and exact 1~N membership/applicability
Per-position stable SDR name/record/entity and BMC-Web row
Whether each channel is discrete presence/fault/status, RPM or another reading
Expected normal state/value, units, tolerance, unavailable/stale semantics and update interval
BMC/SDR/fan-controller firmware versions and polling/rounding allowances
Protected in-band/OOB collection path and credential policy
Thermal/fan abort thresholds, log retention and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Match this source row/variant rather than the duplicate code alone
Never execute or request SF600 flashing for this sensor case
Do not assume every FAN or RPM row belongs to STATUS_UP_FAN 1~N
Enumerate and report each required member separately; do not pass on one representative fan
Retain complete SDR and Sensor List output before filtering; no 60-line cap
Do not change PWM/mode, stop fans, inject faults, reset BMC or clear logs
Protect credentials and stop on missing/stale/invalid status, fan loss, thermal rise or BMC instability
agent_execution_scope: Verify source identity and upper-bank topology
Capture complete read-only SDR and Sensor List inventories
Resolve each owner-approved upper-fan member and normalize status/RPM semantics
Build per-member SDR/Sensor parity and prepare exact Web rows for operator confirmation
Perform no flash, fan control, physical action, fault injection or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the 1~N physical and sensor membership
Define discrete/analog semantics, expected values and freshness rules
Approve Web mapping and unavailable/absent handling
Review every channel and issue the overall result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Read-only `sdr list` can contribute raw data, but FAN/UP_FAN/RPM plus `head -n 60` is overinclusive and incomplete, exposes credentials and omits Sensor List and Web parity. Its SF600 logs/risk are wholly inapplicable and unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through approved secret-safe access, retain complete SDR and Sensor List outputs, select only the owner-enumerated upper-fan records, compare each name/description/status-or-reading with its specification and correlate the exact BMC-Web row.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: STATUS_UP_FAN 1~N, BMC-Web check, three source criteria and 3/3-minute estimates are preserved; membership, sensor type and values are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES UPPER-FAN MEMBERSHIP AND SENSOR SEMANTICS PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map physical upper fans to exact SDR records, collect complete inventories at aligned timestamps, normalize discrete status versus RPM readings, verify all members across IPMI and Web and retain thermal health without stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Completes the source's three-view acceptance path and quarantines an unrelated destructive flash overlay.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A broad filtered list may include lower fans or omit required upper channels; an RPM value cannot automatically satisfy a discrete status criterion, and Web visibility alone cannot prove SDR correctness.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Collection is passive, but a false normal interpretation can conceal cooling loss; any attempt to test by stopping a fan would exceed this row and introduce serious thermal risk.

project_override_considerations: Platforms without an upper/lower bank must provide an explicit mapping or not-applicable decision. Renamed sensors are acceptable only with a versioned physical-to-SDR/Web crosswalk; SF600 remains a separate atomic row.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and three-code-variant separation audit
Per-member SDR record/entity, sensor type, units/state/value/freshness and Web mapping
Versioned expected sensor and thermal specification
Complete redacted raw SDR and Sensor List output with status/timestamps
Per-member normalized comparison and missing/extra/duplicate/stale analysis
Timestamped Web evidence plus passive RPM/temperature/BMC/SEL/OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master test set, Items and criteria consistently describe upper-fan sensor-list coverage; the procedure is incomplete but not contradictory. SF600 content is confined to derived review fields caused by duplicate-code contamination.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The upper-fan monitoring purpose and passive evidence path are identifiable. Membership, semantics and expected values are supplyable platform inputs under ED-36, so the case is not irreducibly blocked.

review_improvement: Quarantines destructive SF600 contamination, converts 1~N into a physical per-sensor completeness matrix and prevents RPM readings or unrelated fan rows from substituting for upper-fan status.
independent_technical_reasoning: The main engineering hazard is dual: code reuse attached a physical flash operation to a passive cooling check, and the range label hides which sensors must exist. `STATUS` may represent a discrete state rather than RPM, so collection must preserve record type and entity before comparison. With an owner-approved upper-bank map, all three source views can be reconciled read-only while thermal health is monitored.
